Interview with Lawrence Brown
by Patricia Willard
Reel Eight

PRO-TYPISTS, INC.
PROFESSIONAL TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE
AREA CODE 202 347-5395
-- when you joined the band in 1932, the drummer was Sonny Greer and (he) remained the drummer all the time until you left in 1951. Tell me a little bit about Sonny Greer?

Oh, Sonny was the personality kid of the band. He was drummer, as you know and was flash -- was flashy. Everything he did was flashy. He had the most beautiful, one of the most beautiful sets of drums in the business when I joined in 1932. And he took great pride in polishing them and keeping them. He had a complete set including timpanies and vibraphones and all kinds of drums and cymbals and chimes, everything. And he really dressed up the band. With his outfit.
They used to seat him -- like the top of a pyramid.
I've heard that he used to sometimes (inaudible) topple backward from his perch up there.
He's a lucky man, he like to broke his neck a couple of times. Off that perch and -- but he was really a showpiece in the band.
I think you were telling me before
that in your opinion Duke learned a lot about showmanship from Sonny, is that right?

Oh, yes, Sonny was, as a -- I said, a personality and he knew so many people and he had different assets that helped him in his work so much. He could remember names from years and would surprise any number of people when they'd come up and he'd call their name right off. How, do you remember me? Which was -- everything (W35) to an advantage.
Did he always speak of himself in the third person, like, "Oh, Sonny knows," like he does now? Or -- he -- "Sonny's here." Did he always talk that way or is that --
I don't remember too much like that. He was -- he was always nice, always jovial and again a member that fit perfectly in the organization.
